title: Polaris Data inference workshop: models & integration
summary: Introductory workshop to map Polaris Data's inference needs. Covered hosted vs dedicated vs private deployment tradeoffs, model candidates (Llama variants, Gemma-style open models, Mistral), context length needs (8k vs 32k), multilingual support, tool-calling requirements, and a pilot/benchmark plan.
topics: open model comparison and quality tradeoffs
next_steps: Redwood to send model performance matrix and sample pricing for hosted vs dedicated
Schedule a 90-minute technical deep dive with Polaris infra team to run a 1-hour benchmark (Samir + Priya + infra) — target week of 2026-08-24
Share SOC2/ISO and KMS integration docs; Polaris to confirm regulatory data residency requirements
action_items: Samir Patel - prepare model perf spreadsheet + cost estimates for 8k/32k context (due 2026-08-18)
Jordan Blake - send draft commercial term sheet and pilot pricing (due 2026-08-17)
Priya Shah - share representative prompt set and sample documents for benchmarking (due 2026-08-20)
transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2026-08-14
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Polaris ML Lead), Marcus Liu (Polaris CTO), Elena Gomez (Polaris Eng Manager)

[00:00:02] Jordan Blake: hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh i'm Jordan from Redwood, i'm the account lead here. with me is Samir our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
[00:00:10] Priya Shah: good, thanks, morning from our side. we've been looking at several open models and wanted to run through fit, specifically around multilingual stuff and the tool-calling patterns we have.
[00:00:19] Marcus Liu: hey all, quick note on timeline — we want something in pilot within the next 6 weeks, depends on ops sign-off.
[00:00:25] Samir Patel: great, that'll shape whether dedicated or private is necessary. quick outline — we'll cover model candidates, expected token/context needs, multilingual tokenization, tool-calling (we saw you mentioned external API calls + DB lookups), and then ops/security questions. sound okay?
[00:00:39] Elena Gomez: yep, works for us.
[00:00:42] Priya Shah: sweet. starting with models — we've tried a few internally, like Llama 2 13B and a 20B open variant. quality for our non-English docs drops off. we care about Spanish, Portuguese, French, and Chinese. also sometimes inputs are long: user transcripts plus doc history, often 12-20k tokens.
[00:00:58] Samir Patel: okay, so context length is real for you. are those 12-20k bursts consistent or occasional?
[00:01:05] Priya Shah: maybe 20% of calls, but important ones. most are 4-6k.
[00:01:09] Jordan Blake: so two axes: average vs tail latency/cost. for average we can optimize batching and caching. for the tails, options are higher context models or stitching techniques.
[00:01:18] Marcus Liu: long ones need to be accurate — we can't drop earlier conversation. how does Redwood handle KV cache or prefix caching?
[00:01:26] Samir Patel: we do automatic prefix/KV caching for repeated prefixes and can keep client-side session KV to avoid resending the whole context. quick caveat — with open models you might sacrifice a bit of raw quality when heavily quantized. but we can route long-context requests to unquantized model variants or larger models on Dedicated.
[00:01:44] [00:02:05] Marcus Liu: can you explain the hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs again? specifically latency and control for PII data.
[00:02:12] Jordan Blake: hosted is fastest for getting started: managed infra, predictable endpoint, pay-as-you-go. dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools — much more predictable throughput and isolation; better for sustained high qps. private (VPC/on-prem) gives you complete control and compliance but longer setup and higher fixed costs. for PII, many customers choose dedicated with customer-managed keys or private if they need air-gapped controls.
[00:02:34] Priya Shah: we have a vendor requirement: data at rest must be encrypted with our KMS and audit logs for model inputs. do you support HSM-backed keys?
[00:02:42] Samir Patel: yes, we integrate with common cloud KMSes and offer HSM-backed options for Private. audit logs are available in Redwood Console with token-level tracing.
[00:02:49] Elena Gomez: is there a difference in latency when you enable KV cache and encryption?
[00:02:55] Samir Patel: minor overhead for encryption at rest; envelope encryption adds negligible request latency. KV cache actually reduces end-to-end latency for repeated prefixes because fewer tokens are generated.
[00:03:05] [00:03:30] Priya Shah: on models — which open models would you recommend for multi-lingual quality and long context? we saw some libs pointing to Mistral, Gemma-ish forks, and LlamaX variants.
[00:03:40] Samir Patel: short answer; Mistral-like and the newer long-context Llama forks are solid. There's also optimized 32k-context variants — some are hybrid architectures. we usually propose a matrix: 1) smaller 13-20B for most traffic, 2) 70B or 32k-context variant for long queries, and 3) a distilled multi-lingual tuned model for languages like Chinese where tokenization hurts.
[00:04:05] Marcus Liu: how do you route those automatically? we need to avoid complexity in-app.
[00:04:11] Jordan Blake: routing's policy-driven. you can set rules based on request size, customer tier, or latency target. Redwood can auto-fallback to a cheaper model if the preferred one is at capacity. we also provide SDK-level helpers so you don't have to implement complex routing.
[00:04:25] Priya Shah: about tool-calling — we need robust function calling for DB lookups and external APIs. sometimes we want the model to call a vector-search tool, get results, then continue generation. is that first-class?
[00:04:35] Samir Patel: yes, we support structured function/tool calling primitives. we have an orchestration hook for tool chains — you can register tools, set auth, and Redwood will coordinate tool call -> update context -> resume generation. small transcription note: sometimes function names get munged in auto transcripts, but in the system they're preserved.
[00:04:55] Elena Gomez: any limitations on tool-calling concurrency?
[00:05:00] Samir Patel: tool calls are external network IO — we recommend async patterns. Redwood can manage timeouts and fallbacks. on Dedicated you can reserve additional capacity for bursts that do heavy tool orchestration.
[00:05:10] [00:06:15] Marcus Liu: okay let's talk cost. what's the delta between running 13B quantized hosted vs dedicated 13B in reserved pool?
[00:06:23] Jordan Blake: approximate numbers up-front: hosted pay-as-you-go will be higher per-token for peak load but zero infra ops. Dedicated reduces per-token by ~30-50% depending on utilization commitments. we'll send a tailored spreadsheet — Samir will include numbers for your expected distro (80% short, 20% long).
[00:06:41] Priya Shah: important — for long-context requests we don't want to double-bill for the same prefix when using KV cache. how does charging work?
[00:06:48] Samir Patel: we bill tokens generated/consumed after caching. if KV cache supplies tokens, they are not re-sent; billing for cache hits is lower. detailed table will be in the perf matrix.
[00:06:58] [00:07:30] Priya Shah: multilingual tokenization: we saw tokenization bloat for Chinese in some models. do you pre-tokenize or recommend subword settings?
[00:07:37] Samir Patel: tokenizer choice matters. some open models use byte-level BPE which helps, but we often recommend a tokenization preprocessing step for Chinese/Japanese to control token counts. for Spanish/Portuguese/French, most models do fine. we'll include tokenization examples with the sample prompts you provide.
[00:07:54] Marcus Liu: thinking about the pilot: we'd like Redwood to run a benchmark on our sample prompt set, comparing 13B/20B/70B models and a 32k context variant. can you run that in a hosted env or do we need Dedicated?
[00:08:07] Samir Patel: we can run the benchmark on hosted for speed — identical models are available there. if you want private data not to leave your VPC, we can set up a Private pilot but takes longer. typically customers start on hosted benchmarks and then move pilot to Dedicated if throughput or compliance requires.
[00:08:22] [00:09:05] Elena Gomez: any gotchas for on-prem? network latency to your control plane?
[00:09:11] Samir Patel: yes, on-prem needs connectivity for the control plane unless you choose an air-gapped package. control-plane chatter is small but initial provisioning and metrics require connectivity. also, on-prem upgrades are coordinated windows.
[00:09:24] Priya Shah: can you talk about model rollouts and version pinning? we can't have silent model drift during critical workflows.
[00:09:30] Jordan Blake: Redwood supports model pinning per route and rollouts with canary percentages. you can tie regressions to eval sets so a model won't be promoted if quality drops. we also keep model artifacts versioned so you can revert.
[00:09:43] [00:10:55] Marcus Liu: security checklist: SSO (SAML), RBAC, audit logs, KMS integration, SOC2 — do you have a one-pager?
[00:11:02] Jordan Blake: yes — we'll send the security pack. quick: SSO via SAML and OIDC, RBAC at workspace and token granularity, full audit logs in Redwood Console, KMS integrations for both Dedicated and Private, SOC2 Type II attestation available.
[00:11:15] Priya Shah: great. one more — data residency. some EU workflows must keep data in EU region. can you pin model serving to specific regions?
[00:11:23] Samir Patel: yes, region pinning is supported; for Dedicated we can provision in specific cloud regions; Private gives full on-prem or VPC control.
[00:11:30] [00:12:45] Elena Gomez: latency SLOs — what's realistic for a 8k prompt on a 13B quantized model?
[00:12:51] Samir Patel: 13B quantized with optimized kernels — p95 generation latency for a 2k token response is typically 200-350ms per 100 tokens after warm-up. for full 8k context, end-to-end latency depends on how much of the context is cached. cold-start for 8k on quantized 13B might be in the 1.2-2.5s range; larger models scale proportionally. we'll include measured numbers in the perf matrix.
[00:13:12] Marcus Liu: hmm, for interactive use we want sub-second for the majority — that's why we think caching and prefix compression are key.
[00:13:20] Samir Patel: exactly — if the long preface is stable, KV caching reduces effective tokenization and runtime significantly.
[00:13:28] [00:14:50] Priya Shah: regarding evals: can Redwood run continuous evals against a fixed prompt set and alert on regression?
[00:14:56] Jordan Blake: yes, Redwood Optimize provides quality monitoring and regression alerts tied to prompt sets; you can configure thresholds to trigger rollbacks or notifications.
[00:15:05] Elena Gomez: any UI for inspecting token-level cost per request?
[00:15:09] Samir Patel: in Redwood Console you get token-level cost breakdowns, model-level latency, and per-route dashboards.
[00:15:15] [00:16:30] Marcus Liu: one practical question: during tool-calling, if a tool returns incorrect data, can we fall back to a different tool or block the model from using the return?
[00:16:37] Samir Patel: yes — orchestration rules let you mark tool calls as mandatory/optional and set fallback logic. timeouts cause optional results to be skipped and generation continues with a note. mandatory failures can trigger error responses or a fallback model.
[00:16:48] Priya Shah: transcription issue — some of our internal tool names have slashes and underscores; will those map cleanly in Redwood function registry?
[00:16:55] Samir Patel: yes, the registry uses canonical names and you can alias. the transcript noise is mostly for the call recorder.
[00:17:10] [00:18:55] Jordan Blake: quick recap of what we'll deliver: a model performance matrix with cost/latency for your distribution, tokenization examples for your languages, SOC2/KMS docs, and a proposed pilot plan.
[00:18:06] Priya Shah: sounds good. for the pilot mechanics: we'll share ~200 representative prompts and some doc attachments. ideally the benchmark shows accuracy and latency metrics across 13B/20B/70B and a 32k variant.
[00:18:16] Samir Patel: perfect — Priya, if you can drop the prompt set to the shared folder, we'll kick off the hosted benchmark and share results within 5 business days.
[00:18:24] Marcus Liu: commercial — what's the pilot cost? small fixed fee or credits?
[00:18:30] Jordan Blake: we typically do a low-cost pilot package for benchmarking — covers compute and engineering time. Jordan to send draft terms.
[00:18:38] [00:20:00] Elena Gomez: regarding deployment complexity — how much engineering effort to move from hosted pilot to Dedicated?
[00:20:07] Samir Patel: on average 2-4 weeks depending on infra integrations, VPC peering, and KMS setup. if you need on-prem, add 4-6 weeks. we'll scope this in the technical deep dive.
[00:20:18] Priya Shah: okay last question — if we want to do model tuning (instruction-tuning on our data), do you support managed fine-tuning?
[00:20:25] Samir Patel: we support fine-tuning workflows and managed fine-tune runs; for sensitive data we recommend doing this inside Private or Dedicated with customer keys. tuned models can be versioned and pinned in Redwood.
[00:20:38] [00:22:40] Jordan Blake: great, unless there's anything else, we'll summarize next steps.
[00:22:45] Priya Shah: one more nit — latency targets differ by client tier. can routing take client_id and pick model accordingly?
[00:22:52] Samir Patel: yes, route by metadata — client tier, prompt length, preferred region; we can make that policy-based.
[00:22:58] Marcus Liu: thanks, this was helpful.
[00:23:02] Jordan Blake: thanks everyone. we'll send the packet and book the 90-minute deep dive for week of Aug 24.

[00:23:30] End of recording

Notes on transcription: occasional misrecognitions (model names like 'Gemma' vs 'GemmaX' may appear slightly off), speaker overlaps, and timestamps approximate. The full meeting audio referenced a shared benchmark spreadsheet and a security one-pager which Jordan will attach in follow-up.
